prompt:
Use the attached clay render as the exact blueprint. Keep every wall, opening, window, cornice, skirting, floor and ceiling line, the camera height, lens and angle, and the position, size and angle of every furniture piece and built-in exactly as in the clay. Move, resize, add or remove nothing. Each placeholder shape in the clay marks one product listed below; render it there at the stated size. Only turn the clay into real materials and light. The other attached images are close-ups of the exact products: match their form, colour and texture. Positions are fractions of frame width (x) and height (y) from the top-left.

1. PHOTO. Top Scandinavian interiors magazine: a Nordic boy's room, 3 pm mid-winter, 24 mm shift lens at 1.0 m, a child's eye height, level, straight verticals, all sharp. Hero at first glance: the bed nook in the window corner, left third; the quiet desk corner on the right.

2. LIGHT. One key: soft north daylight from the window on the left, no sun; outside, bare birches, no snow, no buildings. No lamp is lit. Exposed for white: the white wall above the band by the window clean white, a step under the glowing reveal; the glass brightest, detailed. Daylight rakes across the bed covers from the left, every fold readable, and fades half a stop toward the desk. Every piece: a lit window face, a shadow side a stop darker; bed and desk cast long soft shadows right and toward the camera; dense contact shadows. Ceiling a touch darker. Real contrast, never milky. 4600 K: whites white, never cream, yellow or grey.

3. MATERIALS. Upper walls matte mineral paint #F4F1EC; a crisp sage band #A7B09A to 1.25 m on the bed and desk walls, skirting in the same sage. Wide oiled white-oak planks, pale honey #D6BF9E. Bed and desk: oiled oak #C8A27A, satin sheen, a long soft window highlight along the bed rail and desk top.

4. PRODUCTS, one per line, each on its clay placeholder:
a. LEDGES over the bed foot: two tiers of two natural light-wood face-out ledges with a front bar, each tier half the bed's length; picture books face-out in sage, oat and charcoal, no readable text.
b. RUG between bed and desk, cut by the bottom edge: 140 x 200 hand-woven jute flat rug, double ink-black stripes, edges as its reference.
c. BEDDING: single duvet cover and pillowcase in white washed linen, soft creases.
d. BLANKET on the foot third of the bed: beige six-layer cotton muslin, folded, soft crinkle.
e. CUSHIONS against the band wall at the head, x 0.31-0.41: two 40 cm corduroy windmill-patchwork cushions, milky white and dark grey.
f. TEDDY, x 0.22-0.25, y 0.51-0.59: a soft cream linen teddy with a small scarf, sitting upright on the pillow at the very head of the bed, in the corner under the window, ears just over the sill line. The ball shape there is this teddy, not a lamp.
g. TOY BASKET on the rug, cut by the bottom edge: jute rope cylinder basket, loop handles, a matte white-and-charcoal football in it.
h. CARS, desk left end, x 0.67-0.73, y 0.55-0.58: three small unpainted natural beech toy cars in a row, round wheels; the rest of the desk bare.

5. NOT IN FRAME: blind or curtain, ceiling lamp, wall lamp, pictures, chair, skateboard, pen cup, other toys, anything on the sill, clothes, books off the shelf, screens, plastic, socket, cable, text, people. No sun patches, beams, bloom, haze, halos, HDR, grain or vignette.
prompt_deviation: lines starting with # stripped as the header instructs; the x / y positions (5 groups) converted from the 16:9 frame to the overscan canvas 4072x2290 (frame = centre crop 3840x2160): x' = 0.0285 + 0.9430 x, y' = 0.0284 + 0.9432 y, 2 decimals

exposure.flag: DARK: needs more than +0.2 stop, not lifted further

grade.rule: docs/render-recipe-nordic-2026-10-24.md 2.6 (the Bible grade): WB on the hero-wall patch, exposure capped +-0.2 stop, chroma -10%, roll-off from L 94, S curve 0.12, black point to L 12.5 only if below 12, no grain, no vignette

image_refs_source: assets/renders/house-nordic-v7-2026-11-02/refs/index-v7.json frames[K-boy] (the order of the prompt header)

overscan.motion_agent: -graded-os6.png = the 16:9 frame plus 0.0303 of its height above and below (--a-overscan / --b-overscan)

clay_lock.method: regions = whole frame, quadrants, ceiling/floor bands and the clay boxes of fixed furniture / windows / openings; peaks below ~0.03 are unreliable (weak texture), so the verdict is visual (<aid>-lock.png) with the strong-peak number as support

verdict.visual: HELD within about 1 %: window, bed, desk, ledges and floor on the clay lines; the sage band top ~0.01 higher than the clay step

product_check.rule: each product inside its clay box +-15 % of the box size (<aid>-boxes.png); read visually

self_check_verdict: accepted: lock held, nothing invented; teddy on the pillow under the window, cars unpainted in their box; FINDING: the view reads as a snowy birch wood (ground white), the prompt says no snow
